Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're going through as a new mother, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and if there are any concerns that might need some extra attention. The purpose of this assessment is to check in with you about your emotional well-being during this postpartum period, and it's completely confidential. Everything we discuss is in a safe and supportive space, just for you.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help me get a better sense of how you're doing. These questions are designed to explore your feelings and thoughts over the past 7 days, and they'll give us a good starting point for our conversation. Don't worry; this isn't a test, and there are no right or wrong answers. We're just here to have an open and honest conversation about your postpartum experience.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that you're not alone in this journey. Many new mothers experience a range of emotions, and it's completely normal to have questions or concerns. I'm here to listen, support, and guide you in any way I can.

Let's get started with the first question. Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to be a pretty happy and carefree person, but since having the baby, it feels like everything is just so serious and overwhelming all the time. I do try to laugh and be positive for my baby's sake, but it's just not as easy as it used to be. There are moments when I can laugh and enjoy myself, but they're few and far between. Most of the time, I'm just trying to get through the day and make sure everything gets done. I feel like I've lost a little bit of myself in all of this, and it's hard to find the things that used to bring me joy. Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and for a split second, I'll feel happy and carefree, but then I'll start worrying about something, like if they're eating enough or if they're healthy, and it just brings me back down. So, to answer your question, I wouldn't say I've been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as I used to, and it's really been bothering me.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I wouldn't say that's been me, lately. Like I said, it's been tough to find the humor in things. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and laughing doesn't come as easily as it used to. I'm just so tired and worried all the time, and it's hard to see the funny side of things when you're feeling overwhelmed and anxious. Sometimes I'll watch a funny video or something, and I'll think to myself, "Oh, I should be laughing at this," but it just doesn't feel genuine. It's like I'm just pretending to be happy, but deep down, I'm still feeling really sad and worried. Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

To be honest, not really. I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but lately, it's just been so hard to muster up any excitement. Even things that I used to enjoy, like spending time with friends or trying new restaurants, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, and everything else has kind of fallen by the wayside. I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, and I'll just feel anxious about how I'll manage with the baby, or I'll worry that I'm not doing enough for them, and it just takes all the joy out of it. Sometimes I'll make plans with my partner or friends, and then the day of, I'll just feel so overwhelmed and tired that I don't even want to leave the house. It's like I've lost my sense of purpose and joy, and it's really hard for me to look forward to things like I used to.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's definitely been me lately. I feel like I'm always criticizing myself and wondering if I'm doing everything right. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not feeding them enough or because I'm not changing their diaper fast enough. If they're not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine or because I'm not creating a soothing enough environment. I just feel like everything is my fault, and it's really hard for me to shake that feeling. Even when my partner or family members try to reassure me that I'm doing a great job, I just can't seem to get out of my own head and stop blaming myself. It's like I'm always waiting for something to go wrong, and when it does, I'm like, "See, I knew I wasn't doing this right." It's really exhausting and frustrating, and it makes me feel like I'm just not cut out for this whole mom thing. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeling really overwhelmed and anxious, and I'll just start crying because I feel like I'm failing my baby in some way. It's just really hard for me to be kind to myself and not blame myself for everything that goes wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something ridiculous, like what if the baby stops breathing or what if I accidentally drop them. It's like my mind is constantly racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and it's really hard for me to calm myself down. Even when everything is fine and the baby is healthy and happy, I just can't seem to shake this feeling of anxiety. It's like I'm always looking over my shoulder, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about things like how I'm going to get everything done, or how I'm going to manage on no sleep, or how I'm going to be a good mom. It's just this constant, nagging feeling of worry and anxiety that I don't know how to get rid of. Sometimes I'll try to talk to my partner about it, and they'll just tell me that everything is okay, that I'm doing a great job, but it's hard for me to believe them when I'm feeling so anxious and worried all the time.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, just doing normal everyday things, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes it's triggered by something specific, like a loud noise or a sudden movement, but other times it just seems to come out of nowhere. I'll be feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll feel like I'm going to drop them or hurt them in some way, and I'll just start panicking. It's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no actual threat there. It's really overwhelming and frightening, and it makes me feel like I'm losing control. After it happens, I usually feel really shaken and anxious, and it takes me a while to calm down. It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is just on high alert all the time, waiting for something to go wrong, and sometimes that anxiety just boils over into panic.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely how I've been feeling lately. It's like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a full-time job, and it's exhausting, both physically and emotionally. Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just collapse. I feel like I'm constantly playing catch-up, trying to keep up with the baby's needs, and it's hard to keep my head above water. Even simple tasks, like laundry or dishes, feel like monumental challenges, and I just don't know how to get everything done. I feel like I'm drowning in responsibility, and it's hard to find any time for myself or any sense of peace. My partner tries to help, but it's not the same as being the primary caregiver. I feel like I'm shouldering all of this burden on my own, and it's just getting too much for me to handle. Some days, I just feel like I'm not doing enough, and that's a really hard feeling to live with.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. Even when the baby is sleeping, I'll lie awake at night, feeling anxious and unhappy. My mind just starts racing, and I'll think about all the things that are worrying me, like whether I'm doing a good job as a mom, or whether the baby is healthy, or whether I'm ever going to feel like myself again. It's hard to turn off those thoughts, and it's even harder to relax when I'm feeling so overwhelmed. Sometimes I'll be lying there, feeling really sad and hopeless, and I'll just start crying. It's like my emotions are just simmering under the surface, and as soon as I'm alone with my thoughts, they just boil over. And then, of course, I'll feel guilty for feeling that way, because I know I should be grateful for this beautiful baby, and I am, but it's just hard to feel happy when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and anxious all the time. The lack of sleep just makes everything worse, too. I'll be tired and irritable, and that just makes it even harder to cope with all the emotions that are swirling around inside me. It's like I'm stuck in this vicious cycle, and I don't know how to break free.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, but inside, I'm feeling really sad and miserable. It's hard to explain, because on the surface, everything seems okay. I have a healthy baby, a supportive partner, and a comfortable home. But despite all of that, I just feel this deep sense of sadness and unhappiness. It's like I'm mourning the loss of my old life, my old self. I miss being able to do things spontaneously, to go out with friends, to have time to myself. I miss feeling carefree and happy. Now, everything feels so serious and overwhelming. I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually living. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. I'll be feeding the baby, and I'll just start crying because I'm so tired and overwhelmed. Or I'll be changing their diaper, and I'll feel this wave of sadness wash over me because I'm just so unsure of myself as a mom. It's like I'm constantly questioning my ability to care for this tiny human, and that's a really scary and sad feeling. Sometimes I'll try to talk to my partner about it, but even they don't seem to understand. They'll just tell me that I'm doing a great job, and that I'm a wonderful mom, but it's hard to believe that when I'm feeling so miserable inside.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's happened to me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just crying all the time. It's like the smallest thing will set me off, and I'll just start sobbing. I'll be feeding the baby, and I'll think about how hard it is to breastfeed, and I'll just start crying. Or I'll be changing their diaper, and I'll think about how I'm not doing a good enough job, and I'll just start crying. It's like I'm just so overwhelmed and sad all the time, and it's hard to keep it inside. Sometimes I'll try to hold it in, but it's just too much, and I'll end up crying anyway. It's really embarrassing, too, because I don't want my partner or family members to see me like that. But at the same time, it's hard to hide it, because I'm just feeling so much emotional pain. I'll be crying, and my partner will try to comfort me, but it's hard to explain why I'm crying, because I don't even really know myself. It's just this deep sense of sadness and unhappiness that I don't know how to shake. And the worst part is, I feel like I'm crying for no reason, like I'm just being ridiculous and overreacting. But at the same time, it feels like my body is just releasing all this pent-up emotion, and it's hard to stop it once it starts. It's really scary, too, because I don't know how to make it stop, or how to feel better. I just feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of sadness and crying, and I don't know how to break free.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

No... I don't think that's something I've considered. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've wondered how I'm going to get through this, but I don't think I've ever thought about harming myself. I think I've just felt more like I'm not doing a good enough job, or that I'm not cut out for this whole mom thing, but I don't think I've ever had thoughts of self-harm. I've just felt really sad and hopeless, like I'm stuck in this rut and I don't know how to get out of it. But I don't think I've ever thought about doing anything to hurt myself. I think I've just felt more like I need help, like I need someone to talk to or some way to make these feelings go away. I've felt like I'm just barely holding it together, but I don't think I've ever had thoughts of self-harm.

As a new mom, you're experiencing a range of emotions and challenges that are common during the postpartum period. You've shared feelings of sadness, anxiety, and overwhelm, which are impacting your daily life and relationships. It's essential to acknowledge that these feelings are valid and deserve attention and support.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 27, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>the 'Not at all' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have hardly looked forward with enjoyment to things lately, stating they've lost their sense of purpose and joy, and things they used to enjoy no longer seem appealing.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong tendency to self-blame, even when reassured by others, and experiences frequent feelings of failure and guilt, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a high level of anxiety and worry, describing themselves as 'always on edge' and experiencing 'constant, nagging feelings of worry and anxiety' that are difficult to shake, even when things are fine.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, quite a lot' option.</sym>, <sym>the guideline option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all'.</sym>, <sym>Patient reports difficulty sleeping due to feeling anxious, unhappy, and overwhelmed, indicating a high level of unhappiness affecting their sleep most of the time.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have been feeling sad and miserable a lot lately, and that it's a persistent feeling that they can't shake off, matching 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>Yes, most of the time</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's responses indicate a high level of emotional distress, consistent with symptoms of <med>postpartum depression</med>. The EPDS score of 27 suggests a probable depression, which warrants urgent referral to a <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>. The patient's symptoms, including <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, and <sym>loss of pleasure in activities</sym>, align with <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>PCP</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage <med>support groups</med> for new mothers
3. Discuss <med>therapy options</med>, such as <med>cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)</med> or <med>interpersonal therapy (IPT)</med>
4. Explore <med>medication options</med> with a <med>healthcare provider</med>
5. Develop a <med>self-care plan</med> to manage stress and emotions
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 27: **Postpartum Depression Screening Summary**

The patient presents with a range of symptoms and emotional/behavioral concerns that warrant further evaluation. Main symptoms expressed include persistent sadness, loss of pleasure in activities, and difficulty coping with responsibilities. Consistent patterns across answers include low mood, anxiety, guilt, and feelings of being overwhelmed.

**Screening Significance:**

* Postpartum depression: Patient reports persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells, which are consistent with symptoms of postpartum depression.
* Postpartum anxiety: Patient expresses anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed, which may be indicative of postpartum anxiety.

**Risk Factors:**

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of guilt and worthlessness
* Anxiety, panic, and being overwhelmed
* No reported thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation

**Screening Observations:**

The patient reports significant emotional distress and difficulty coping with responsibilities since the birth of their baby. They express feelings of sadness, guilt, and anxiety, which are impacting their daily life and relationships. While the patient denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation, their reported symptoms and emotional concerns suggest a need for further evaluation and potential support.

**Recommendations:**

Further assessment and evaluation are recommended to determine the severity of symptoms and develop an appropriate plan for support and treatment. Referral to a mental health professional or support services may be beneficial to address the patient's emotional and psychological well-being.
